summary: Retest of the iteration_96 CRITICAL regression (Radar touch-lock permanently 'hidden'). The fix replaced pinch/pan onBegin/onFinalize with pan's raw onTouchesDown/onTouchesUp/onTouchesCancelled hooks as the sole interaction-lock signal. Confirmed via a fresh demo login (login-demo button) and direct DOM/console instrumentation that the underlying bug is STILL PRESENT: onTouchesDown fires reliably on mouse/pointer-down (interaction lock engages, ScrollView overflow correctly goes to 'hidden' and RefreshControl is removed), but onTouchesUp does NOT fire when the pointer is released while still over the Radar element (the normal case for a tap or a drag-then-release-in-place) - confirmed by adding a temporary console.log inside onRadarInteractionStart/End in app/(tabs)/index.tsx: after mouse-down+up in place, only 'onRadarInteractionStart, count=1' logs, no matching 'onRadarInteractionEnd' ever fires, even after 5s wait. radarTouchCount never returns to 0, so scrollEnabled stays false and RefreshControl stays removed forever - identical symptom to iteration_96, just with a different root cause (onTouchesUp not firing on release-in-place, rather than pinch/pan double counting). onTouchesCancelled does appear to fire IF the pointer is dragged completely off the element bounds before release (count decremented in that specific case), but this is not the common tap/drag-and-release path. Repeated 5x consecutive touch-down/up cycles on radar-map - ScrollView overflow stayed 'hidden' every time, never recovered (0/5). Debug code was reverted after diagnosis; expo restarted clean. Smoke-retest of previously-passing behaviors (no regression there): zoom +/- buttons correctly step the focus chip 4->16 tiers, recentre correctly resets to 4, Radius/Events/Filters sheets open and close normally.

integration_issues.flow: Radar touch-interaction lock (radarInteracting) - RadarView.tsx pan.onTouchesDown/onTouchesUp/onTouchesCancelled wired to app/(tabs)/index.tsx onRadarInteractionStart/onRadarInteractionEnd
integration_issues.issue: STILL CRITICAL / NOT FIXED: onTouchesDown fires correctly on touch-down (lock engages, ScrollView scrollEnabled=false, RefreshControl removed - correct). But onTouchesUp never fires when the pointer/finger is lifted while still over the Radar (the normal tap/drag-release case), so radarTouchCount never decrements back to 0 and the outer ScrollView + pull-to-refresh remain permanently disabled for the rest of the session after the very first touch. Reproduced 5/5 consecutive touch-down/up cycles via mouse simulation (matching the same technique used in iteration_96) plus confirmed at the JS level with a temporary console.log instrumentation showing onInteractionStart fires but onInteractionEnd does not, even after a 5s wait. onTouchesCancelled DOES appear to fire, but only if the pointer is dragged fully outside the element's bounds before release - not the common case.

action_items: The root-cause fix in this round did not actually resolve iteration_96's bug - it changed which callback is unreliable, not the underlying reliability problem. onTouchesDown fires but onTouchesUp does not fire for the typical release-over-element gesture in this app's react-native-gesture-handler version (~2.32.0) on web. Investigate whether this is a react-native-gesture-handler-web limitation for onTouchesUp/onTouchesCancelled on the Pan gesture specifically (search suggests some RNGH web touch-event support requires 'needsPointerData' config or a newer/experimental web implementation flag) - verify on a REAL native device/simulator (iOS/Android), not just web preview, since web RNGH touch emulation may differ from native.

Given TWO consecutive fix attempts (onBegin/onFinalize ref-counting, then onTouchesDown/Up/Cancelled) have both left the counter stuck > 0 after release, strongly consider a more defensive design: (a) add a hard safety-timeout (e.g. setTimeout 400-800ms after onTouchesDown/onInteractionStart) that force-resets radarTouchCount to 0 and radarInteracting to false if no matching onInteractionEnd arrives, so a stuck lock self-heals instead of being permanent, and/or (b) don't gate scrollEnabled/RefreshControl removal on a manual JS ref-counter across GestureDetector callbacks at all - investigate using GestureDetector's own gesture composition (e.g. Gesture.Native() blocking, or NativeViewGestureHandler disallowInterruption) which is handled natively rather than reconstructed in JS.

Retest specifically on a native iOS/Android build or Expo Go if possible, since this bug may be web-preview-specific (RNGH web touch event support gaps) rather than present on real mobile - but as of this web-preview retest, the bug that this fix was supposed to resolve is unresolved from a QA standpoint.
critical_code_review_comments: RadarView.tsx pan gesture's onTouchesUp/onTouchesCancelled are the sole source decrementing radarTouchCount, with zero redundancy or timeout-based recovery. Any single missed/unfired onTouchesUp call (confirmed happening in this test environment) permanently locks the outer ScrollView with no self-healing path - the parent screen (app/(tabs)/index.tsx) has no safety net (e.g., a max-wait auto-reset) for this exact failure mode, despite this being the second consecutive round where the counter got stuck.

No unit/integration test exists asserting radarTouchCount returns to 0 after a start/end pair - this class of bug (asymmetric event pairing) has now caused 2 regressions in a row and would benefit from an automated regression test once a native testing harness is available.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Login: go to /login, click [data-testid=login-demo] (Explore Demo) - lands on /today already authenticated, then click [data-testid=tab-radar]. Dismiss ping popups via get_by_text('Dismiss', exact=True) in a retry loop after login and after switching tabs. To reproduce the touch-lock bug: get radar-map bounding box, page.mouse.move to center, mouse.down(), wait ~150ms (state should show scroll container overflowY='hidden' - lock engaged, correct), mouse.up(), wait 1-5s - overflowY stays 'hidden' forever (bug). Scroll container found via: walk up from [data-testid=radar-map] parentElement chain until getComputedStyle().overflowY is 'auto'/'scroll'/'hidden'. For deeper JS-level diagnosis, temporarily add console.log inside app/(tabs)/index.tsx's onRadarInteractionStart/onRadarInteractionEnd (revert after) - this proved onTouchesDown fires (count increments) but onTouchesUp never fires on release-in-place (count never decrements), while onTouchesCancelled fires only if the pointer is dragged fully outside the element bounds first.
rca_of_issue: The new fix (pan.onTouchesDown/onTouchesUp/onTouchesCancelled replacing pinch/pan onBegin/onFinalize) assumed RNGH's raw touch lifecycle hooks are always symmetric (1 down = 1 up/cancelled per finger) regardless of platform. In this web-preview test environment (react-native-gesture-handler ~2.32.0 running via react-native-web), onTouchesDown reliably fires on pointer-down, but onTouchesUp does not fire when the pointer is released while still within the gesture's target bounds (the common tap/drag-release case) - confirmed via direct console.log instrumentation (onInteractionStart logs, onInteractionEnd never does, even after 5s). Only onTouchesCancelled seems to fire, and only when the pointer/finger is dragged entirely outside the element bounds before release. Net result: radarTouchCount increments on every touch but essentially never decrements back for a normal tap/drag/release, so the ScrollView lock introduced to protect in-progress pinch/pan gestures never releases and the whole Radar tab becomes permanently unscrollable with pull-to-refresh disabled after the very first touch - the same end-user-visible symptom as iteration_96, caused by a different but equally real callback-firing asymmetry.
